summary: The record protocol holds on the Orin (sm_87): the two-half seqlock read, the fold with its ver guard, straggler ordering and the run-time grouping check are all sound. I found no lost, duplicated or misattributed effect and no deadlock in them under H1-H6. The late-pointer-writer mechanism (R3.6) does not hold as written. (1) Blocking: the flip is not sticky. UNIT_ADD and host writes set slot hints back to LIVE, and new slots start LIVE, so deferral resumes after the SYNC store and D5 becomes unbounded again; T22 fails. (2) CPU programs attach in loop 1 of init_attach_ctx_from_handlers, before the scan, hint store and fold, which are placed between the loops. (3) After a flip caused by a GPU atomic writer, every UNIT_ADD replaces the element. With the stripe's spare being reused, the writer's later atomics are lost or land in another key, with no time bound and in no listed deviation. The other gaps: the B == 0 path (extra_buffer = 0, used in other contexts) has no staging word, lock or gen, yet slice 1's retprobe unit B has a register delta. The context rule covers only write_trampoline_globals; try_loading_ptxs (the late path after a refresh) and run_attach_entry_on_gpu (its own cuCtxCreate) also write map_info. Owner liveness by (pid, start time) judges a live owner in another pid namespace as dead, and retiring its ledger loses its commits. Minor: the retire has no CAS; the pre-Volta no-spin claim is wrong; R9 wording; an all-zero key can match an empty cache entry; T22's oracle contradicts D5; losing the context inside a live process has no rule; the pointer-writer scan misses writes made by helpers. All checks were by reading code. The only extra run was llc-15 on the red-team IR.
checked_ok: R3.4 two-half seqlock read (Lemma 1): the writer alternates half[((v>>1)+1)&1] and bumps ver odd then even with membar.sys. The reader reads half[c&1] and accepts if v2 <= 2c+2. Checked for v1 even (2c) and odd (2c+1): the half it reads is overwritten only after a store of ver=2c+3 followed by membar.sys, so by MP (H2) a reader that saw new half bytes sees ver >= 2c+3 after its fence. It never waits, and the snapshot is the state current at the v1 load. This needs the CPU fence between the half loads and the second ver load to be a load-load or acquire fence.

R3.4 fold ver guard: a fold that reads a record older than the watermark (no H6, another process folded under the same stripe lock) stops before computing a delta, so nothing wraps. The guard works whether the watermark keeps v1 or 2c. An odd v1 with unchanged c gives Δcount = 0, a no-op.

Stragglers for UPSERT and IF_PRESENT, including a straggler followed by a UNIT_ADD on the same key. The next group takes L after the straggler's leader releases it, and its membar.sys before flag1 (default_trampoline.cu:157-158) is cumulative, so the watcher's fold-before-serve applies the straggler first (re-create, then add). A straggler cannot be hb-before the host operation it lands after: Lemma 2 plus H2. A section hb-after the host op's hint store reads the new hint (H3).

R3.4 CPU-probe and loader fast paths are sound provided the fold publishes the watermark with release after changing the element and the fast path loads it with acquire. Slot creation zeroes the record, so a slot created during a read shows no movement.

R3.3 grouping check on sm_87 (ITS). Lanes that get the same m from activemask executed it together, so shfl.sync and vote.ballot.sync(m) are well formed. Lanes that do not reconverge, or that arrive from another call or round, only form smaller groups: performance, not exactness. Exited lanes and partial warps are excluded. Each lane is in exactly one G, and every lane of G has equal (fd, site, key), so they share one B and one L. Non-leaders wait at the first syncwarp(G) until the leader holds L, so staging adds happen only under the group's own lock, and hash collisions only serialize. bar.warp.sync orders the adds before take(). The leader's membar.sys plus syncwarp(G) puts the commit before later host calls of every lane in G.

Nested host_call inside a leader section (UNIT_ADD while holding L): activemask inside host_call returns only lanes at that PC, so the turn loop's __syncwarp(active) cannot wait on a lane parked at syncwarp(G). The lock order is always L, then the module comm lock, then occupy_flag. No CPU path in slice 1 holds a stripe lock while waiting on the GPU (no flip kernel), so there is no deadlock on sm_87.

nomerge below the IR: I ran llc-15 -march=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_61 on redteam/sink-nomerge.O3legacy.ll (output in /tmp/claude-2002/-home-jetson-src/6ac0883f-4479-466c-bec5-5fa31cffe4de/scratchpad/recheck/out.ptx). It keeps 4 calls; sink.O3legacy.ll keeps 2. NVPTX codegen does not re-merge this sample. ptxas was not tested, and the check makes it irrelevant for correctness anyway.

Lane-turn fallback: n = 1 per lane under its key's lock inside today's turn loop (default_trampoline.cu:143-175) is exact. The trampoline's PTX is .version 8.1 (trampoline/Makefile) and already uses bar.warp.sync and activemask, so shfl.sync and vote.sync acceptance is very likely.

R3.2 context premise: the segment is registered with CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_DEVICEMAP|PORTABLE (bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1462-1464). write_trampoline_globals writes globals in the current context, or the primary when there is none (nv_attach_impl.cpp:2306-2310, 2366-2385). Helpers 1-3 read extra_buffer only for ARRAY and GPU types (default_trampoline.cu:238-272), so a device-block pointer in a HASH entry does not change them. Per-context library globals mean a library first used in another context sees zeroed map_info (a pre-existing crash through constData = 0), not a foreign device block.

R3.8 citations hold: the alive set is filled after init (agent.cpp:1119-1121 then 1195-1196; 724-726 then 731-733) and emptied at detach (463-473). The last detach waits at most 2 s (nv_attach_impl.cpp:160-167). refresh_attach_session destroys every link and re-runs init (agent.cpp:701-727). A refresh switches the old patched probes off (nv_attach_impl.cpp:2393-2405), which narrows D5's straggler window.

Retire-on-death with a correct death verdict: the fold before retiring plus the ver guard make concurrent loader folds harmless, an odd ver left by the dead owner is read through its committed half, and the new ledger starts from zero records, so totals continue exactly.

issues.section: R3.6 (flip step 1) with R3.4 (UNIT_ADD step 4, host writes)
issues.problem: The slice-1 flip is not sticky. It stores SYNC into the existing slot hints once, but every later hint writer stores LIVE again, and new slots start LIVE. The GPU decides only on devmode (fixed in slice 1) and the slot hint, so deferral resumes right after the flip. D5's bound and T22 fail, which reopens red-team issue 4.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:461: the flip stores SYNC into every slot hint of M. DESIGN.md:423: UNIT_ADD step 4 says 'Find or create the slot; set the hint; return the slot'. DESIGN.md:417: host writes 'set the hint (LIVE, or ABSENT ...)'. DESIGN.md:367-369: the GPU tests only `devmode != DEFER || h != LIVE`. Interleaving: (1) agent B finds the late uprobe `*v = 0`, stores SYNC in every slot of M, folds, attaches. (2) A GPU group on key k reads SYNC and sends UNIT_ADD. (3) The watcher serves it and 'sets the hint', to LIVE. (4) The next group on k reads LIVE and commits a record. (5) Any reader folds by replacement (the D5 rule). replace_locked makes the old element the stripe's spare (bpftime_hash_map.hpp:510-538: 'A value pointer from a lookup stays on the old element, which the next update in that stripe reuses'), so B's `*v = 0` through its pointer is lost. Steps 2-5 repeat for as long as the program runs. A first touch of a new key creates a LIVE slot, and a loader update also stores LIVE. The flip's SYNC stores are not under the stripe lock, so even a flag-checking writer could overwrite one.
issues.fix: Add a FLIPPED bit in the ledger header, set before step 1. Every hint writer (UNIT_*, host writes, slot creation) checks it under the stripe lock and writes SYNC instead of LIVE or ABSENT. Step 2's per-slot fold re-stores SYNC under each stripe lock, which closes the check-then-store race. The flipped ledger stays attached to the handler so stragglers are still folded. Extend T22 and M21: after the flip, run a UNIT_ADD on an existing key and a first touch of a new key, and assert that no record ver moves for sections that start after the hint store.

issues.section: R3.6 / R7 'Where' (scan placement)
issues.problem: The scan, hint store and fold run between the two instantiation loops, but CPU programs' links are attached in loop 1. A late CPU pointer writer therefore attaches and runs before the flip, while the owner's GPU still defers with LIVE hints. Step 3 ('then lets the new program attach') cannot hold. The window is the rest of loop 1 plus the analyzer (unmeasured per R7), not 'one device-lock section', and late_stragglers does not count it.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:127 and :454 place the scan between the loops. Loop 1 is bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:229-245 with handle_nv_attach_impl=false. instantiate_handler_at (:355-379) calls instantiate_bpf_link_handler_at, and only CUDA programs are deferred to loop 2 (:619-656). Non-CUDA links attach at :676 (create_attach_with_ebpf_callback) in loop 1. refresh_attach_session (agent.cpp:701-727) and agent start (agent.cpp:1119-1121) both use this order. Interleaving in agent B: loop 1 attaches uprobe P (`v = lookup(k); ... *v = 0`). P's lookup takes the fast path (no movement). A GPU unit commits +5. P then observes something hb-after that commit and stores 0. B's scan flips and folds in place, so k = 5, while SR (commit end hb store) gives 0.
issues.fix: Run the pointer-writer scan, the hint store and the fold before loop 1. The scan reads only handlers and needs no CUDA context (DESIGN.md:458). Alternatively, attach links of flagged CPU programs only after the flip. State the placement in R3.6, R7 and the 'What changes' table.

issues.section: R3.6 (flip caused by a GPU atomic pointer writer) / R1 deviations
issues.problem: After such a flip, UNIT_ADD applies every add by element replacement. The late GPU program does atomics through pointers taken from call 1. Each replacement sends its later atomics to a retired element, which the stripe reuses for another key. Effects are lost from k and misattributed to another key, for as long as the writer stays attached, and in no deviation: D5 covers only sections that read LIVE before the hint store.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:465: 'UNIT_ADD applies its add by replacement too'. replace_locked (bpftime_hash_map.hpp:528-538) links the new value in the stripe's spare and sets st.spare = old_index, and the next update in that stripe reuses the old element. The late program's lookup returns a segment address (default_trampoline.cu:277-283, served at bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:134-141). Interleaving: (1) the late program's lookup(k) returns p = &e. (2) A rewritten unit on k reads SYNC and sends UNIT_ADD; the replacement links e' and makes e the spare. (3) The loader updates k2 in the same stripe, which reuses e. (4) atomicAdd(p, 1) lands in k2. In SR the unit replays as an in-place lookup plus atomic add (DESIGN.md:181), so k should hold that +1. Instead k misses 1 and k2 gains 1.
issues.fix: Either list this as a new counted deviation (unbounded while a GPU atomic writer is attached, with misattribution within a stripe) or keep the element in place. For example, after a GPU-writer flip UNIT_ADD returns the element's device address, as MAP_LOOKUP does, and the leader applies sigma with a GPU atomicAdd, so the add meets the writer's atomics in one atomicity domain. Keep replacement only for straggler folds, which are bounded.

issues.section: R3.3 pseudocode / R3.2 context rule (B == 0 path)
issues.problem: The B == 0 path (no device block: modules in another context, other agents) is said to run UNIT_* per group. But the staging sum, the lock and the route to the ledger header (gen) all live in or through the device block. For a non-immediate delta, the group sum sent with UNIT_ADD is undefined, and so is gen. Slice 1 has such a unit (the cuda-counter retprobe, B with d = r7, runs on the Orin), and T21 asserts exactness in another context.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:331: the lock table entry holds {lock, staging sum} in the device block. DESIGN.md:352: non-immediate deltas are summed by atomicAdd into staging(L). DESIGN.md:357 and :338: B == 0 goes to 'UNIT_* per group'. DESIGN.md:363: `L = &B.locktab[...]` is computed from B. DESIGN.md:369 and :420 put gen in the request. MapBasicInfo (default_trampoline.cu:84-92) has no gen field. DESIGN.md:551 gives shape B d = r7. T21 is DESIGN.md:817.
issues.fix: Specify the B == 0 path. After the agreement check, the leader gathers each lane's delta with shfl.sync over G's set bits (sm_30-level, the same primitive as the check), or the path uses lane-turn with n = 1. Carry gen in the descriptor immediates or a new MapBasicInfo field. Make T21 use the retprobe unit (non-immediate delta).

issues.section: R3.2 context rule / 'What changes' / T21, M20
issues.problem: The rule (extra_buffer = 0 when the load context differs from the block's) is attached only to write_trampoline_globals. Two other paths copy map_basic_info into modules unfiltered, and in both the device block can be used from another context.
issues.evidence: fatbin_record::try_loading_ptxs (nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:251-292) calls cuModuleLoadDataEx in the current context, then cuMemcpyHtoD of impl.map_basic_info. It is the late path used after every refresh (nv_attach_impl.cpp:2081, 2100). Its context comes from ensure_cuda_context_for_current_thread (:1851-1855), which keeps any current context, for example an application thread calling bpftime_agent_control. run_attach_entry_on_gpu (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1316-1349) always makes its own context with cuCtxCreate and copies this->map_basic_info. bpftimetool cuda calls it after init_attach_ctx_from_handlers (tools/bpftimetool/main.cpp:244-262) in a process that opens SHM_OPEN_ONLY and registers the segment (bpftime_shm_internal.cpp:1070), so it runs the global step and can own a ledger. A rewritten helper 600 there dereferences a primary-context block. Neither file is in 'What changes', and T21/M20 cover only cuLibraryLoadData.
issues.fix: Mark ledger entries (a MapBasicInfo flag or a side list). Have one helper used by all three writers set extra_buffer = 0 unless the current context is the block's. run_attach_entry_on_gpu always gets 0. Extend T21/M20 to the late path.

issues.section: R3.8 owner identity and death
issues.problem: Liveness by (pid, start time) read from /proc in the reader's pid namespace judges a live owner in another pid namespace as dead. The design itself names cross-namespace pid reuse as the alive set's flaw. Slice 1 then retires the live owner's ledger, and its GPU keeps committing: either the drops are counted as dead_drops, though D2 covers only closed maps, or they go into a retired ledger that no reader folds. Separately, pid and start time survive exec and the incarnation is not part of the test. After the owner image exec's, the owner looks alive forever, and deferral silently stays off for that run. If self-rejoin is keyed on pid plus start time, the new image would reuse a device pointer from a destroyed context.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:494: 'dead when that process is gone or its start time differs' and '... pids are reused across pid namespaces'. DESIGN.md:496: slice 1 folds, marks DEAD and creates a new ledger. DESIGN.md:368: DEAD means drop. Interleaving: the owning application runs in a container with its own pid namespace, sharing /dev/shm. A host-side agent starts, reads /proc/<owner pid>/stat, finds nothing or another process with a different start time, and retires the ledger. The owner's next commits are dropped or never folded.
issues.fix: Base liveness on a resource the kernel releases at exit. The owner holds a lock on a per-ledger file, opened O_CLOEXEC, for its lifetime (or a robust mutex in the segment), and another agent declares death only when it can take that lock. This works across namespaces and across exec. Alternatively, record the owner's pid-namespace inode and never retire across namespaces. Use the incarnation id for self-rejoin. Add a T19 variant with the owner in another pid namespace.

issues.section: R3.8 retire-on-death (slice 1)
issues.problem: Retiring is not atomic. Two agents that start after the owner died can both create a new ledger and both install it. The loser's GPU commits go to a ledger no reader folds, or both agents defer into one ledger with separate shadows, so a record has two writers.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:496 has no CAS; a CAS appears only in slice 2's takeover (DESIGN.md:497). DESIGN.md:340-343: one writer per word. The pre-existing CommSharedMem zeroing by every agent (bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:615) already makes two GPU agents unsafe, hence minor.
issues.fix: Retire with a CAS on (owner identity, ledger pointer) in the map handler. The loser uses UNIT_* through the host-only bit.

issues.section: R3.3 Properties ('no intra-warp spin on pre-Volta')
issues.problem: The peeling loop lets one group's leader lock or call the host while the rest of the warp continues. Two groups of one warp spin on each other when they share a lock entry: the same key on two sites, or keys colliding in hash & (NL-1). They also spin when one leader holds the module comm lock during UNIT_ADD. Without ITS, if the SIMT stack runs the not-in-G path first, the second leader spins forever. On sm_87 (ITS) this is starvation-free, so slice 1 on the Orin is not affected.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:362 and :382. default_trampoline.cu:146-149 (module comm lock, occupy_flag). host_call avoids this with lane turns and __syncwarp(active) (default_trampoline.cu:126-175).
issues.fix: Close each round with a barrier: every lane of m stays in the loop, G commits, then __syncwarp(m) before the next round, as host_call does. Otherwise drop the pre-Volta claim and limit R8 to sm_70+.

issues.section: R9 'Return probes and divergence'
issues.problem: R9 says groups come from activemask, which contradicts R3.3 and Lemma 3: groups come from the run-time agreement check, never from activemask.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:733 versus DESIGN.md:255 and :347. The kretprobe pass inserts the call before every ret and exit, including predicated ones (ptxpass_kretprobe/main.cpp:56-60), so lanes reach the probe from different call sites.
issues.fix: Reword: groups are formed by the agreement check over the lanes activemask reports.

issues.section: R3.2 key-to-slot cache
issues.problem: The cache is verified by comparing key bytes with index[s]. An empty, zeroed cache entry reads {key 0, slot 0}, and an index slot not yet created reads key 0. The micro unit's key is 0. This is safe only if a never-created slot's hint is not LIVE, but the hint states (LIVE, ABSENT, DEAD, SYNC) have no 'none' value and no encoding. If LIVE were 0, key-0 commits would go to slot 0's record. Slot creation later zeroes that record (loss), and the next key given slot 0 inherits the shadow totals (misattribution). There is also no bounds check on s.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:333 (verification against the index), DESIGN.md:327 (records zeroed at slot creation), DESIGN.md:575 and :767 (key 0).
issues.fix: Add an occupied bit to index and cache entries, or define hint 0 = NONE. Check s < C before indexing.

issues.section: R10 T22 versus D5
issues.problem: T22's oracle ('no CPU store lost after the hint store') contradicts D5, which allows a straggler fold by replacement to lose a write through an old pointer. The test provokes exactly that case (late_stragglers > 0). For CPU writers, replacement is also unnecessary: an in-place aligned 4/8-byte atomic add is single-copy atomic against the uprobe's aligned plain stores and its atomics.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:818 versus DESIGN.md:233-235. bpftime_hash_map.hpp:510-538: the old pointer stays on the retired element.
issues.fix: For flips caused by CPU writers, fold stragglers in place; T22's oracle then holds. Keep replacement only for GPU atomic writers (see the replacement issue above), or restate T22 to exempt pointers older than a counted replacement.

issues.section: R3.8 ownership versus context lifetime
issues.problem: Ownership ends only at process exit, but the device block and its shadows belong to the primary context. cudaDeviceReset or cuDevicePrimaryCtxReset in a live process destroys them while the records keep ver 2c and their totals. Reusing the old pointer faults. A fresh block restarts shadows at ver 0 and totals 0, so the fold guard ignores the new commits, or the delta goes negative.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:329 and :495. Takeover seeding (DESIGN.md:497-499) is slice 2 and covers only process death.
issues.fix: Record the block's context id (cuCtxGetId) and treat a change as owner death: retire in slice 1, seed in slice 2.

issues.section: R3.6 pointer-writer scan
issues.problem: The scan flags only store and atomic instructions through a lookup pointer. A lookup pointer passed to a helper that writes through its argument violates PW with no flag and no flip. On the CPU: bpf_probe_read*, bpf_get_current_comm and similar. On the GPU, helper 503 writes through its three arguments.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:455-456 and :156-159. default_trampoline.cu:511-517 (helper 503 stores through x, y, z).
issues.fix: Count a lookup pointer, or a pointer derived from one, passed to any helper with a writable pointer argument as a pointer write.

summary:
I re-read the whole DESIGN.md and checked it against 52126f33 (llvmbpf 87bac39a). Nearly every path:line in "The model in one page", R3.2, R3.3, R3.4, R3.6, R3.8, R7 and R10 says what the document claims. I reran exec_mode.py and its output is byte-identical (35/21/3, slice 1 20 → 14 on the Orin), and the CUDA Counter arithmetic (8 → 3 removed → 5) holds against the source. The design is still not consistent with itself or with the code in slice 1:
- **Hints go back to LIVE after a flip (blocking).** UNIT_ADD and host writes set hints back to LIVE after the hint-store flip. Deferral then resumes on a map with a pointer writer, and the D5 bound fails.
- **No sweep in slice 1 (blocking).** Without it, a straggler re-creation is invisible to get_next_key, so T4 and the observation-point claim fail, and capacity can deviate more than D4 says.
- **Scan runs too late (major).** The pointer-writer scan runs between the two loops, but loop 1 has already attached CPU links.
- **Leftovers that trust the static group (major).** R4-A, R5 and R9 still describe a static group path, Σ = popc, and groups from activemask.
- **M17 is not guaranteed to fail (major).** With nomerge in the build, T18 may still pass under M17.
- **Build list and test list disagree (major).** Examples: gen/DEAD and NOSLOT are built but T7 and T8 are deferred; T16 and T15 are in neither slice; T22's oracle contradicts D5; M15 is detected through a tally R7 says is not a check.
- **R10's plumbing cannot produce several numbers (major).** No readback for "32 × launches", "total = Σ deltas" or "Σ sm = Σ warp"; a 120 s victim timeout; no harness for the CPU-probe and loader-lookup overhead.
- **Minor items:** wording, cost accounting and citations.

The in-place rewrites fit, checked against the disassemblies:
- **cuda-counter entry A** (pc 22-37): LBB0_2 (30) is targeted only from 27 and LBB0_3 (38) only from 29, so no jump fixups are needed.
- **Retprobe B** (28-35 plus nops at 36-42 and 69-76): LBB1_3 (69) only from 32, LBB1_4 (76) only from 42, the printk path 43-68 only from 16, and r10-0x28 is read at 107.

Mechanisms that check out:
- **Seqlock.** The two-half read with accept if v2 ≤ 2c+2 is correct against the writer order in R3.3: the writer of commit c+2 is the first to touch half[c&1], so a read is never torn and never waits.
- **Lock order.** It is L → module lock → occupy_flag, and the watcher never waits on the GPU, so slice 1 has no deadlock.
- **First-touch races** on one key serialize through L and the stripe lock.

issues.section: R3.4 (Host writes; UNIT_ADD step 4) vs R3.6 (late pointer writers), D5
issues.evidence:
DESIGN.md:417: host writes "set the hint (LIVE, or ABSENT plus the absent list)". DESIGN.md:423: UNIT_ADD "Find or create the slot ...; set the hint". DESIGN.md:461: the flip only stores SYNC into existing slot hints. R3.3 pseudo-code line 369 defers whenever devmode == DEFER and h == LIVE.

Interleaving:
1. Ledger M (UPSERT_ADD, e.g. sm_histogram) has LIVE slots.
2. T22's uprobe P (`*v = 0` through a lookup pointer) appears. The agent stores SYNC into all hints, folds, attaches P.
3. A warp on a key k' with no slot yet (a new SM or warp key) misses the cache and sends UNIT_ADD. The watcher creates the slot and sets hint[k'] = LIVE. The same happens on any loader bpf_map_update_elem of an existing key.
4. Later sections on k' read LIVE with devmode still DEFER and commit records. They started after the hint store, so D5 does not cover them: late_stragglers is either 0 or unbounded.
5. Folds after the flip apply by replacement (R3.6:465). P's `*v = 0` through a pointer taken before such a fold lands in the retired element and is lost. T22's "no CPU store lost after the hint store" fails with no early straggler involved.

The same happens when a UNIT_ADD reads "not flipped", the flipper stores SYNC, and UNIT_ADD then stores LIVE.

issues.section: R10 "Not in slice 1" (the sweep) vs R1 observation points, D4, Lemma 4, T4
issues.problem:
Slice 1 drops the sweep on the grounds that "no slice-1 unit deletes". But host deletes of ledgered keys still happen in slice 1 (T4 print-and-clear, T11), and R3.4 says stragglers after a host delete re-create the key.

Without the sweep, a pending re-creation is invisible to get_next_key. R1:191 relies on get_next_key sweeping, so the observation-point claim (R1:189) fails, and T4's oracle fails when its final dump iterates.

Capacity also deviates more than D4 admits: D4 (229-232) and Lemma 4 (257-260) assume count-changing operations sweep first, and only straggler order is listed as remaining.
issues.evidence:
Iteration case:
1. Key k has slot s and hint LIVE.
2. GPU section G loads LIVE while holding L.
3. The tool runs lookup_and_delete(k): fold, delete, hint ABSENT.
4. G commits Δ to s after that fold's read (a straggler, ordered after the delete; R3.4:425-428).
5. The kernel ends. The app syncs and exits, and the tool waits on it, so the commit's end hb the dump's start.
6. The final dump calls get_next_key(NULL). k is absent from the base map, and nothing folds s, because no sweep exists in slice 1 (DESIGN.md:769). k is not listed: Δ is in neither "returned" nor "final", and T4's Σ returned + final = N·L fails.

This is the dump pattern the cuda-counter loader itself uses (cuda_probe.c:45-56).

Capacity case:
1. The map is full except k's place; a straggler for k is pending.
2. Commit end hb a host insert of j (a CPU probe in the app after cudaDeviceSynchronize).
3. The insert succeeds, because no sweep runs.
4. A later fold of k finds the map full and drops Δ.

SR orders the commit before insert(j), so it requires k re-created and E2BIG for j. That is more than D4's "which ones get in follows sweep order".
issues.fix:
Keep the absent-list sweep in slice 1. It is O(absent list) and already specified:
- in get_next_key when it starts at the first key or at a missing key;
- before count-changing host operations near capacity.

Otherwise, state a slice-1 deviation explicitly (iteration may miss pending re-creations; inserts may take the capacity a pending re-creation needed), with a counter, and make T4 read "final" by direct lookups of every key it has seen. Either way, restate Lemma 4 for slice 1, and move T12 or a small-map variant into slice 1.

issues.section: R3.6 (step 3 "then lets the new program attach"), R7 "Where", What changes (row 1)
issues.problem:
The pointer-writer scan, hint store and fold run "between the two loops" of init_attach_ctx_from_handlers. But loop 1 already attaches CPU links. A late CPU pointer writer is therefore live, with hints still LIVE and folds in place, before the step that is supposed to precede its attach.

PW (R1:156), on which Invariant I and Lemma 2 rest, is violated in a window R3.6 says does not exist. T22's oracle starts "after the hint store", so it cannot see the window.

The R3.6 citation is also wrong: the auto-refresh thread does not go through refresh_attach_session. It calls init_attach_ctx_from_handlers directly, without destroying links.
issues.evidence:
In loop 1, bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:229-243 calls instantiate_handler_at(..., false). That reaches instantiate_bpf_link_handler_at (:376), which attaches non-CUDA links at :656-686 without testing handle_nv_attach_impl, and inserts them into instantiated_handlers (:695-696).

The auto-refresh thread calls init only (agent.cpp:754-785 at :777, and :1155-1191 at :1183). It never calls destroy_all_attach_links, unlike refresh_attach_session (:721-726).

Interleaving:
1. Agent X owns M's ledger.
2. A second loader adds a uprobe P (`*v = *v + 1` or `*v = 0` on M) linked into the same process.
3. X's auto-refresh runs init. Loop 1 attaches P, and P fires.
4. Only after that does the global step store SYNC and fold.

The same happens when another process's agent starts.
issues.fix:
Run the pointer-writer scan, the hint store and the fold-all before loop 1. Per R3.6:458 they need only segment handlers and no CUDA context. Alternatively, defer CPU links of programs that the scan flags until after the step.

Then update the "What changes" row and R7 "Where", and correct the R3.6 citation: list the auto-refresh thread's direct init calls (agent.cpp:777, 1183) as a separate entry point. Extend T22 to attach P through auto-refresh.

issues.problem: Three places still describe a static grouping path that trusts the analysis or activemask. R3.3 and Lemma 3 forbid that, and the red team's issues 1 and 15 were closed against it. An implementer following R5 would build exactly the M17 mutation.

issues.section: R10 tests and mutations: T18 / M17 vs the nomerge hunk in the slice-1 build
issues.problem:
M17 (no grouping check, trust popc(activemask)) is supposed to fail T18. Slice 1 builds the nomerge hunk, and with nomerge the IR keeps the two sibling units as separate calls (re-run: 4 → 4). Under M17, T18 then fails only if NVPTX/ptxas merges the calls or ITS reconverges lanes of both call sites inside the non-inlined helper. The document lists both as open (R3.3:348, open question 6).

So M17 may survive, and the exit criterion "their mutations fail" cannot be met deterministically.
issues.evidence:
DESIGN.md:349, 762 (nomerge in slice 1), 814 (T18), 842 (M17), 852 (exit criterion), 874 (open question 6).

The opt-15 rerun: sink-nomerge.ll keeps all 4 calls to `_bpf_helper_ext_0600`.
issues.fix: Make T18 force the merged call so the agreement check is what it exercises. Build T18's fixture without the nomerge hunk, or with a hand-written IR/PTX unit whose single call has a `select`ed site and fd, as in redteam/sink.O3legacy.ll. Keep a separate nomerge check that counts calls in the kept PTX ("PTX kept", R10).

issues.section: R10: slice-1 build list vs "Slice 1 runs" vs mutation table vs exit criteria
issues.problem:
The build list and the test list disagree.
- **gen/DEAD:** built in slice 1 (item 4), but its test T7 and mutation M10 are deferred "with slice 2's pieces", although gen and DEAD are slice-1 pieces.
- **NOSLOT/ledger-full fallback:** built (R3.4 UNIT_ADD step 4, helper 600), but T8 is deferred.
- **T16 (divergent return probes):** in neither slice, though slice 1 rewrites the cuda-counter retprobe B units its exit criterion depends on. T15 is likewise in neither slice.
- **T22's oracle** ("no CPU store lost after the hint store") contradicts D5, which allows exactly that loss for late stragglers applied by replacement.
- **M15** is said to fail via "T17 shows 20/38/1", the class tally that R7 says is reported, not used as a check.
issues.fix:
Move T7/M10, T8 and T16 into the slice-1 run list, or move gen/DEAD and NOSLOT out of the build list. Assign T15 to a slice.

Condition T22's oracle: "no CPU store lost unless it overlaps a counted late straggler; late_stragglers ≤ sections in flight at the hint store". Restate M15's expected failure as "T17 reports an exec_mode mismatch at cudagraph:56".

issues.section: R10 Build item 7 (measurement plumbing) vs "Expected numbers" and "Exit criteria"
issues.problem: Item 7 names modes and config entries only. Several numbers in the expected-numbers table cannot be produced with what it names.
issues.evidence:
The gaps, row by row:
- **"32 × launches" for hash-lookup-present and hash-counter:** the micro loader only selects programs and sleeps (benchmark/gpu/micro/cuda_probe.c:52-127, 179-181), so nothing reads key 0 or the pid key back. hash-counter also needs a new BPF program, which is not named.
- **CUDA Counter "total = Σ deltas":** the loader reads only call_count (example/gpu/cuda-counter/cuda_probe.c:37). Σ deltas exists only in the printk lines.
- **threadscheduling "Σ sm = Σ warp":** threadscheduling.c prints the SM total (:64-117) but only the first 20 warp entries, with no warp total (:137-175). "2 commits per group" needs the statistics dump, which is not in the build list.
- **hash-counter at 1,024 / 100,352 threads, "today" side:** the presets run 10,000 and 1,000 iterations (micro_vec_add_config.json, small and large), about 113 s and 1,070 s at 11 ms and 1.07 s per launch. The runner kills the victim at 120 s (run_cuda_bench.py:229-235).
- **"CPU-probe lookup on a ledgered HASH" and "CPU-probe and loader-lookup overhead reported":** the second is an exit criterion. No harness is named. benchmark/uprobe (uprobe.bpf.c, diagnostics/hash_map_path_layers.cpp) times unledgered maps and has no fixture that creates a ledger.
- **Placement:** the new micro modes belong in micro_vec_add_config.json, where the CPU Hash cases are. Item 7 cites only examples_vec_add_config.json:22-62.

issues.section: R10 Expected numbers, threadscheduling row
issues.problem: "1 host call + 2 commits per group" understates the host calls. The thread_mapping SET (F) stays synchronous per lane in slice 1, so a 32-lane group still makes 32 host calls per launch, not 1.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:781. records-exec.json gives threadscheduling:86 (F) exec_mode_slice1 = "sync_per_lane (today)". The call itself is threadscheduling.bpf.c:86.
issues.fix: Write "1 host call per thread (thread_mapping) + 2 commits per group (sm, warp) + one UNIT_ADD per new key".

issues.problem: The text says 14 slice-1 sites "run on the Orin". That count includes threadscheduling_dynamic_hook's 4 sites, which R10 leaves out of the measured set. Slice 1 measures 10 sites: micro 1, cuda-counter 5, threadscheduling 4.

issues.section: R3.1 "Never needed"
issues.problem: The line lists "GPU atomics on the segment" as never needed. Every UNIT_* fallback in slice 1 goes through host_call, which does GPU atomicCAS and atomicExch on occupy_flag inside CommSharedMem in the registered segment. The line's own parenthetical concedes occupy_flag is GPU-only.
issues.evidence: default_trampoline.cu:149 (`atomicCAS(&comm->occupy_flag, 0, 1)`), :167 (`atomicExch(&comm->occupy_flag, 0)`). DESIGN.md:308.
issues.fix: Say "no new GPU atomics on the segment beyond today's GPU-only occupy_flag lock", or list it as an existing, already-exercised precondition.

issues.section: The model in one page "Facts" vs R3.1 / R10 step 0 gate; slice-1 build list

Two inconsistencies about the start-up facts:
- **Three-party facts:** the model says deferral is off unless the facts hold, including the three-party ones. R3.1 and the step-0 gate enable deferral on H2-H4 alone; a failed H6 only restricts (rt) to pairs.
- **No start-up gate in slice 1:** "litmus-tested at start-up" (and R8's cached start-up parameters) has no item in the slice-1 build list. Slice 1 relies on the one-time step 0.

issues.section: R3.3 Properties (Cost), R8 cost model
issues.problem: The verified key-to-slot cache added after the red team needs at least one more uncached system-memory load per commit: the slot's key bytes in the CPU index. The cost line and the cost model still count 1 uncached load.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:333 ("compares the key bytes with the slot's entry in the CPU index"), 364, 383 ("1 uncached load"), 713 ("c_atom_dev + c_ld_sys + ...").
issues.fix: Count 1 + ceil(ks/8) uncached loads (hint plus key words) in R3.3 and R8, and measure that in c_commit in step 0.

issues.section: R3.4 fold guard and "Watermarks := snapshot"
issues.problem:
The text never says which `ver` the watermark stores.

If an implementation stores v2 from an accepted read where v1 = 2c and v2 = 2c+2, the watermark claims commit c+1 while holding commit c's totals. The guard then skips the next read at ver 2c+2, so commit c+1 stays unfolded until a further commit, which breaks (rt) for the last commit of a run.
issues.evidence: DESIGN.md:390-391, 395, 402. The accept rule allows v2 = 2c+2.
issues.fix: State it: the watermark ver = 2c, the snapshot's own commit index (or v1). Never v2. Add that case to T20.
